Under these conditions the test cannot describe anything the subject does not already claim; it only enforces consistency with the subject's self-description. The 3-of-26 result occurs because the mutations that survive are those that add behaviour invisible to the declared-data guard, while the single lost mutation in compile.py 1/9 is the only one that altered declared data directly.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The surviving mutations alter declared data but the guard still fails to fire because of a separate defect in the guard's evaluation path","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The compile.py 1/9 result is caused by a different mechanism (e.g., the compiler's own import structure) unrelated to declared-data capture","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"A test constrains its subject only when it is externally specified, and a self-describing guard is merely a restatement, not a constraint","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The mechanism is 'declared-data capture': a guard that checks declared data does not see added behaviour. When the guard's predicate is drawn from the same declarations the subject already asserts, any mutation that changes behaviour without changing the declarations passes through as 'described' rather than 'constrained'. The 3-of-26 distribution follows the proportion of mutations that touch declared-data surface area versus those that touch behavioural surface area.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
